transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-23
Time: 15:00 - 15:45 UTC
Duration: ~45 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Lee (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Alex Martinez (Orion Head of ML), Nora Chen (Orion Platform), Samir Patel (Orion AI Eng)

Auto-summary (auto-generated):
- Quick review of this week's benchmark runs; Redwood and Orion compared synthetic latency/throughput across hosted vs dedicated pools.
- Decision leaning toward pinning rwd-llama-70b-v2-q4f for most traffic, with fallback to rwd-llama-13b for tail spikes.
- Action items: share updated spreadsheet, run dedicated 1k-sample latency test, provide traffic shape.

Topics: model selection, version pinning, rollback/fallback policy, KV cache behavior, dedicated throughput, security/privateness concerns

--- Transcript ---
[00:00] Jordan Lee: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, I think we have about 45 minutes, thanks for squeezing this in. quick round of intros?
[00:12] Alex Martinez: Hi Jordan, Alex here, Head of ML at Orion. Nora and Samir are with me.
[00:18] Nora Chen: Nora, platform eng, hi.
[00:21] Samir Patel: Samir, AI eng, thanks.
[00:25] Jordan Lee: Great. Priya from Redwood -- Priya, you want to say hi?
[00:29] Priya Nair: Hey all, Priya Nair, solutions engineer. We'll jump into the benchmark results and model pinning proposals.
[00:36] Jordan Lee: Quick agenda: review last week's runs, discuss pinning options and fallback, confirm next steps.

[00:40] Priya Nair: So first slide, the benchmark sheet Jordan shared — link: https://short.url/rwd-orion-bench (note: internal link) — we ran the 5k synthetic and the 1k sam- — sorry, 1k real sample subset from Samir's production traces. The hosted api results show median token latency at 220ms for rwd-llama-70b-v2 quantized on our hosted pool. Tail (95th) is 480ms.
[01:05] Samir Patel: I noticed the 95th spiked around the same time we had caching misses. I think our prefix distribution is skewed.
[01:12] Priya Nair: Yeah, we saw KV cache misses on several long-context cases; the runtime currently evicts older KV entries when memory pressure rises, which for your longer sessions caused misses. We suggested increasing the KV cache slot count in the config — that reduces cold-start token overhead.
[01:30] Alex Martinez: When you say Kv cash, do you mean KV cache? The transcription spelled it weird — but yeah, we saw that.
[01:37] Jordan Lee: (laughs) yeah, KV cache. So two levers: more KV cache and pinning a heavier quantized model vs fallback chain.

[01:50] Priya Nair: On model choices: our recommendation this week is to pin rwd-llama-70b-v2-q4f for your main route because it gives best quality for long-form product descriptions. For cost/throughput, we propose fallback to rwd-llama-13b-quant if latency spikes or GPU pool is saturated.
[02:10] Nora Chen: How aggressive is that fallback? We don't want sudden model swapping mid-request.
[02:16] Priya Nair: Fallback is at request routing level — it triggers only when queue depth or latency SLO breach thresholds are reached; it won't swap mid-request. For in-flight requests we have graceful degradation: keep serving on same variant until completion.
[02:33] Alex Martinez: Can we do a canary? say 5% traffic on 70b-v2-q4f then ramp?
[02:39] Jordan Lee: Absolutely. Our rollout supports canary percent and automatic rollback based on latency and quality regressions. We can set automatic rollback if quality metric (BLEU/ROUGE surrogate) drops >2% or latency >25% from baseline.

[02:55] Priya Nair: One nuance: quantized 70b has slightly different tokenization edge-cases in our infra; we caught a small hallucination in the TOS test where a date got misformatted — we logged it in the sheet. It's rare but wanted to call it out.
[03:15] Samir Patel: Hmm, that's concerning for our compliance use-cases. Are hallucination rates measured in the benchmark?
[03:21] Priya Nair: We run a small eval set — we have a 'quality delta' column. The 70b quant has +1.2% quality improvement over 13b on your eval, but one-off hallucination we saw is likely prompt engineering related.
[03:33] Alex Martinez: Can we run an eval that mirrors our long ticket threads? Those are the problem areas.
[03:38] Jordan Lee: Yes, that's one of the next steps — Samir to send a 500-sample from ticket threads, Priya will run it against the 13b and 70b pin candidates and share results.

[03:55] Priya Nair: On throughput: dedicated pool numbers — Priya speaking — on a reserved Redwood Dedicated pool with 8xA100 equivalents, we saw sustained 60 tokens/sec per GPU for 70b quantization in our runs; total qps depends on batch size and prefix distribution. For your traffic shape we project needing ~10 GPUs to handle peak.
[04:20] Nora Chen: That's more than we budgeted for on dedicated. Any cost-lowering options?
[04:25] Jordan Lee: A few options: batching limits, more aggressive prompt trimming, or using 13b for lower-cost routes like quick summaries. Also mixed-pinning — pin 70b for premium customers, 13b for standard.
[04:40] Alex Martinez: Mixed pinning makes sense. For rollout, we want pin 70b for 20% of traffic first (premium) then reevaluate.

[04:52] Priya Nair: About the pinning config itself — we recommend: route-level model pin pinned_model: rwd-llama-70b-v2-q4f, fallback_chain: [rwd-llama-13b-q4] with policy: fallback on queue_depth>50 or observed latency>400ms for 30s window. Canary: 5% initial, auto-ramp to 20% over 48h if no regression. We also add an automated rollback window of 2 hours on regressions.
[05:22] Samir Patel: Does the fallback preserve token-cost accounting and attribution for billing?
[05:26] Jordan Lee: Yes we log per-request model variant and token delta, so billing can be attributed by route/model. We can provide a cost breakdown per-route in the console.

[05:35] Nora Chen: Security question — for the dedicated pool, how are keys managed? We use customer KMS.
[05:41] Priya Nair: For Private and Dedicated we support customer KMS/HSM integrations; logs can be routed to your SIEM. We also have SOC 2 Type II and can provide audit log retention options.
[05:52] Alex Martinez: Good. Also need to confirm data residency — some data must stay in EU region. Can we pin region?
[05:58] Jordan Lee: Yes, routing supports region pinning; you can enforce region=eu-west1 in the route.

[06:05] Priya Nair: Back to the benchmark: the hosted run had slightly better tail latency because of our multi-tenant pooling. Dedicated had more predictable median but tail varied based on batch sizing. There's a configuration tradeoff: if you set very small max-batch  to reduce tail, throughput drops.
[06:26] Samir Patel: We need a baseline cost per 1M tokens for each model/pool so we can present to finance.
[06:31] Jordan Lee: We'll add per-1M token cost lines in the spreadsheet. Jordan to share pricing vs committed capacity and spot rates.

[06:44] Alex Martinez: Any notes on rollback — how fast is rollback if we detect quality regression?
[06:49] Priya Nair: Automated rollback can be near-instant for routing changes (secs), but if you need to switch pinned model that requires a config update which propagates in ~30-60s across edge routing. In practice, end-to-end rollback happens in under 2 minutes.

[07:05] Nora Chen: A question about metrics — can we tie quality regressions to specific prompt sets so we don't roll back globally for a narrow prompt break?
[07:12] Priya Nair: Yes, you can scope evals to prompt sets. We support rolling back only for routes where the regression triggered, and tagging regressions to the eval suite that failed.

[07:24] Jordan Lee: Let's talk about the one-off hallucination Priya mentioned: it's in row 23 of the sheet; the prompt had both a date and legal clause, and the model rephrased the clause incorrectly. Priya, did you try prompt templating?
[07:40] Priya Nair: We added a guardrail with a structured output schema for that prompt type. It reduced hallucinations on the 100-sample retest. Will include the template in the sheet.

[07:55] Alex Martinez: Good, please include that. We'll want to test again with our ticket threads.

[08:05] Samir Patel: Regarding KV cache, what are recommended defaults? We saw defaults were too low for 2k context sequences.
[08:12] Priya Nair: For long 2k sequences we recommend increasing kv_cache_slots to 4096 (from default 1024) on dedicated; for hosted we can adjust TTL-based retention. There's a memory tradeoff which we can quantify.

[08:30] Nora Chen: If we increase KV cache slots memory usage goes up; will that trigger higher GPU counts for dedicated?
[08:36] Priya Nair: Slightly, but it's usually marginal. The bigger driver is sequence length and batch size. We'll simulate memory pressure in the 1k-sample dedicated test.

[08:50] Jordan Lee: On observability, you'll get per-token breakdowns, slow request traces, and the route dashboards. Priya, do we have a sample trace to show?
[08:59] Priya Nair: Yes, link to a sample trace in the sheet. We'll attach the trace export to the ticket.

[09:10] Alex Martinez: Ok next, how do we handle version pinning when we do model upgrades — e.g., rwd-llama-70b-v2 -> v3?
[09:17] Priya Nair: We recommend creating a new model variant in the catalog and then a controlled canary rollout. The system keeps previous variant in the fallback chain so rollback is simple. We also tag each model with a single-document changelog we surface in the console.

[09:30] Samir Patel: Any risk that newer weights will change tokenization or cause downstream QA regressions?
[09:36] Priya Nair: There can be small tokenization deltas; we run a regression harness that checks token alignment and a sample of live prompts. You can opt-in to a stricter eval policy for critical routes.

[09:50] Jordan Lee: Let's capture concrete plan: 1) Jordan shares spreadsheet update by Wednesday (2026-03-25). 2) Samir sends 500 ticket-thread samples by Friday (2026-03-27). 3) Priya runs 1k dedicated latency + KV cache memory sim by Thursday (2026-03-26) and publishes logs. 4) We'll set up a 5% canary on rwd-llama-70b-v2-q4f then ramp to 20% if metrics pass.

[10:20] Nora Chen: Timeline sounds good. One thought — can we include a finance rep on the next call to talk committed capacity?

[10:26] Jordan Lee: Yes, we'll invite finance next week.

[10:30] Alex Martinez: Also need security to review KMS integration notes; I'll open a security ticket.

[10:36] Jordan Lee: Great. Any other questions?

[10:40] Samir Patel: One small thing — in the hosted run we saw jitter around midnight UTC, could be noisy traffic. We'll mark those traces and exclude from baseline.

[10:50] Priya Nair: Good call. We'll filter by traffic bin when we compute baselines.

[11:00] Jordan Lee: Alright thanks everyone. We'll follow-up with the sheet and run results. Calendar for next weekly sync same time next week?

[11:07] Alex Martinez: Works for us.

[11:10] Jordan Lee: Thanks, bye.
